title: Is the Digit String an Additive Sequence?

concept.title: Guess the first two numbers, then the rest is forced
body: An *additive sequence* has at least three numbers and every number from the third one on is the **sum of the two numbers before it**, like `1, 99, 100, 199`. A string of digits is additive if it can be cut into such a sequence. Once the first two numbers are chosen, the whole rest of the string is **forced**: the next number must be their sum, and the sum must appear in the string right there.

So the search is only over the **lengths of the first two numbers** (two nested loops). For each choice the check `follows` is a recursion that either succeeds or fails at the first mismatch. Numbers may not have leading zeros (a number `0` is fine, `01` is not). The numbers stay below 10^17 here, so sums fit in a 64-bit integer.

statement: A string of digits is *additive* if it can be cut into at least three numbers (no number has a leading zero, except the number 0 itself) so that every number after the first two is the sum of the two numbers before it. Decide whether the given string is additive.
inputFormat: The only line has the digit string.
hints: Try every length for the first number and for the second number.
The next number must be the sum of the last two; write it as text and check that the string continues with it.
A number with more than one digit must not start with 0.

explanation: For each pair of lengths of the first two numbers (without leading zeros), the following numbers are forced: each must be the sum of the previous two and must appear in the string at the current position. The string is additive if one choice consumes it all.
solution.complexity: Time O(n^3) at most, space O(n).
